commit.message:
feat(dm): surface swallowed DAO bookkeeping failures via reporter port (#4402)

* feat(dm_repository): add error reporter port for swallowed bookkeeping failures

`DmRepository.recoverSelfWrap` and `_finalizeAfterRecipient{Success,Failure}`
swallow DAO writes via `Log.error` only. With #4241 invoking
`recoverSelfWrap` on every app-foreground transition, we need a production
signal for how often these doubly-degraded paths fire — without crossing
the `dm_repository` → app package boundary.

Introduces `DmRepositoryErrorReporter` (a typedef) as an optional
constructor parameter. Each of the 7 swallow sites — outer-transaction
catch in `sendMessage`, the rumor JSON parse path, the deleteById
fallback, the doubly-degraded bookkeeping sink, both post-publish
markSelfWrapStatus failures, and `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure` — now
invokes the reporter after `Log.error`. The previously-silent inner
swallow after JSON parse also gains a matching `Log.error` so the
unified log stays consistent.

Sites are addressed via `DmRepositoryReportableSites` constants so the
Crashlytics dashboard aggregates per site. The doc on the typedef makes
the contract explicit: reporters must not throw.

Tests extend `createRepository` with a recording-closure reporter and
add assertions to the existing swallow-path tests plus three new tests
covering the otherwise-uncovered finalizeAfterRecipientFailure swallow,
the sendMessage outer-transaction swallow, and the previously-silent
markSelfWrapStatus-after-JSON-parse swallow.

Coverage: 94.21% (above the 93% gate).

Refs #4127

* feat(dm): wire DM bookkeeping failure reporting to Crashlytics

Forwards the new `DmRepositoryErrorReporter` port to
`CrashReportingService.recordError` inside `dmRepositoryProvider`, with
`reason: 'DmRepository.<site>'` so the Crashlytics dashboard aggregates
per swallow site.

`OutgoingDmRetryService` gains an optional `CrashReportingService?`
constructor parameter (singleton-default, matching `DivineBlocObserver`)
and reports the two existing `Log.error`-only catches — per-row
`recoverSelfWrap` unexpected throws and the top-level sweep failure —
via the new `OutgoingDmRetryServiceReportableSites` constants.

`ConversationBloc._onSelfWrapRecoveryRequested`'s `addError(lastError,
…)` is upgraded to `Reportable(lastError, context:
'_onSelfWrapRecoveryRequested')` so the bloc-level failure flows through
`DivineBlocObserver` to Crashlytics. Single migrated site → string
literal per `error_handling.md` (1 site → literal, 2+ sites → constants
class).

Tests:
- `outgoing_dm_retry_service_test.dart` adds a `_MockCrashReportingService`
  and two tests verifying both swallow sites report to Crashlytics with
  the correct `reason:` annotation.
- `conversation_bloc_test.dart` updates the existing `errors:` assertion
  from `isA<StateError>()` to the `Reportable<Object>.unwrap →
  StateError` form per the matrix migration recipe.

Refs #4127

* chore(dm): regenerate app_providers.g.dart after dmRepositoryProvider change

Updates the provider hash for `dmRepositoryProvider` to reflect the new
`errorReporter` closure in its factory. The CI `Generated Files` job
caught this — Riverpod codegen needed to be re-run after the factory
body change.

Refs #4127

* test(dm_repository): drop unused wireErrorReporter flag in test helper

The `wireErrorReporter` parameter on `createRepository` was added with
a `true` default but no test ever passes `false`. Removing per
code_style.md ("if you are certain something is unused, delete it
completely"). All tests still get the recording reporter wired —
`reporterCalls` resets per-test in `setUp`, and tests that don't trigger
a swallow simply observe an empty list.

Refs #4127

* fix(dm): stop retrying terminal self-wrap recovery races

* test(ci): skip optimization for global-state upload tests

---------

Co-authored-by: Liz Sweigart <127434495+NotThatKindOfDrLiz@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
feat(dm): recoverFullSend primitive + auto-sweep wiring for recipient-failed DMs (#4410)

* feat(dm): add recoverFullSend primitive for recipient-failed outgoing_dms rows

Closes the recovery gap for `outgoing_dms` rows in
`recipient_wrap_status: failed`. Today the retry service from #4241
enumerates these rows but cannot act on them — only the
`recipient: sent / self: failed` case has a recovery primitive
(`recoverSelfWrap`, PR #4106). Without this, an app kill or relay
reject that finalized as recipient-failed leaves the row indefinitely
broken even after connectivity restoration.

`DmRepository.recoverFullSend(rumorId)` mirrors `recoverSelfWrap`'s
shape: validates ownership, idempotent-defers to `recoverSelfWrap`
when the row's recipient wrap is already sent (a concurrent recovery
or the original partial-success path), rebuilds the rumor from
`rumor_event_json` (preserving the receiver-side dedup key across
retries), calls `sendRumor`, then finalizes via the existing
`_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` / `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure`
helpers. The success transaction persists `direct_messages` + upserts
the conversation row + deletes the queue row atomically, mirroring
`sendMessage`'s happy path.

Re-publishing a rumor whose original wire copy actually landed is
safe: NIP-17 receiver-side dedup keys on the rumor id, which the
stored `rumor_event_json` preserves verbatim. Minting a fresh rumor
on retry would defeat that contract.

Relates to #3909. Closes the design portion of #4240; the
strategy-table wiring in `OutgoingDmRetryService` ships in the
following commit.

Tests cover full delivery, partial delivery, recipient failure,
idempotent recipient-sent defer, missing row, foreign owner, missing
DAO, rumor JSON parse failure, and degraded local-persistence-after-
publish-success.

* feat(dm): wire recoverFullSend into OutgoingDmRetryService strategy table

Second commit in the #4240 stack. PR #4241 left
`recipient_wrap_status: failed` rows in a counting-only branch with
the inline comment `recovery primitive lands in #4240`. With the
primitive now in place from the prior commit, the sweep dispatches
those rows to `DmRepository.recoverFullSend` instead of merely
incrementing a log counter.

Strategy table after this change:

  recipient: sent / self: failed → recoverSelfWrap
  recipient: failed              → recoverFullSend
  pending: pending               → not in retryable filter
                                   (interrupted-send recovery deferred)

The dispatch reuses the existing per-row backoff, `_isSweeping`
re-entrancy guard, and the StateError/ArgumentError/unexpected-throw
error policy from the `recoverSelfWrap` branch.

The sweep summary log gains `full-send-recovered` and
`full-send-failed` counters, replacing the now-acted-on
`recipient-failed=N` log line. The obsolete `#4240` comment in the
class doc is removed; the doc now states both strategy entries.

Tests update:
- `does NOT dispatch recipient: failed rows` becomes `dispatches
  recipient: failed rows to recoverFullSend` since the contract
  inverted.
- The `contract: never republishes recipient wraps` group is renamed
  to `dispatches the correct primitive per row state`. The strict
  invariant now reads "no `sendMessage`/`sendGroupMessage` for any
  retryable row" — `sendRumor` flows through `recoverFullSend`
  intentionally for `recipient: failed` rows (the whole point) so it
  can no longer be in the `verifyNever` list.
- New tests pin: `recoverFullSend` never invoked for
  `recipient: sent` rows; per-row backoff still applies; StateError
  aborts pass without bumping retry; ArgumentError is terminal-skip;
  unexpected throw bumps retry and continues.

Closes #4240. Relates to #3909.

commit.message:
perf(inbox): remove N+1 latest-message overlay queries in DmRepository (#4408)

* perf(inbox): remove N+1 overlay queries; fix write-path drift (#4296)

- Replace per-conversation getMessagesForConversation(limit:1) fan-out
  in _overlayLatestMessages with a single batched
  getLatestMessagesForConversations query (Option A). Inbox emit cost
  drops from O(n) DAO reads to 1 regardless of conversation count.

- Fix write-path drift in ConversationsDao.upsertConversation: the
  last_message_* columns are now only updated on conflict when the
  incoming timestamp is strictly newer than the stored one (Option B).
  This prevents out-of-order gift-wrap arrivals during backfill from
  overwriting a fresher denormalized preview. A forceUpdateLastMessage
  escape hatch is used by _refreshConversationPreview (post-deletion)
  where the replacement message is by definition the newest remaining.
  currentUserHasSent is also now a write-once ratchet at the SQL level.

- Keep _overlayLatestMessages as a transitional read-path safety net
  for existing user databases that may have stale rows from before the
  write-path fix. Removal tracked in #4407.

- Add 4 new ConversationsDao unit tests covering: out-of-order upsert
  does not overwrite a newer preview; in-order upsert does update;
  forceUpdateLastMessage bypasses the timestamp guard; currentUserHasSent
  is never flipped back to false.

- Update dm_repository_test stubs and verify calls to include the new
  forceUpdateLastMessage parameter where _refreshConversationPreview
  is exercised.

* refactor(inbox): unify upsertConversation via DoUpdate.withExcluded

Replace the two-branch (forceUpdateLastMessage) implementation with a
single unified DoUpdate.withExcluded path that applies the same metadata
semantics regardless of the force flag:

- participantPubkeys, isGroup, isRead: always overwritten
- subject, ownerPubkey, dmProtocol: coalesce (keep existing if incoming null)
- currentUserHasSent: one-way ratchet (OR of old and excluded)
- lastMessage*: iif(previewCondition, excl.col, old.col) where
  previewCondition is either 'incomingIsNewer' (default) or true (force)

This removes the raw hand-written INSERT...ON CONFLICT SQL that
duplicated the schema column list and eliminates the latent bug surface
from having two incompatible update contracts behind the same method.

* test(inbox): cover upsert conflict contract

---------

Co-authored-by: Liz Sweigart <127434495+NotThatKindOfDrLiz@users.noreply.github.com>
